## Line parallel to HP and inclined to VP

Consider a straight line **AB of true length 8 units**, parallel to the
horizontal plane (HP) and inclined at **45° to the vertical plane (VP)**.
This example uses **first-angle projection**, with AB above HP and in front
of VP: the front view is above the XY reference line and the top view is below it.
Lower-case labels $a,b$ denote the top view; $a',b'$ denote the front view.

Since AB is parallel to HP, its top view shows both its **true length** and
its **45° inclination to XY**. Its front view is parallel to XY and is
foreshortened:

$$
ab = L = 8, \qquad a'b' = L\cos\phi = 8\cos45^\circ \approx 5.66\text{ units}.
$$

Here $\phi=45^\circ$ is the inclination to VP, while the inclination to HP
is $\theta=0^\circ$. Both views must have the same horizontal endpoint
separation, $\Delta x=L\cos\phi$. The change in distance from VP is
$\Delta y=L\sin\phi$, and the change in height above HP is $\Delta z=0$.
For positioning only, A is taken 2 units in front of VP, and both endpoints
are 3 units above HP. B lies farther in front of VP than A.

```{python}
#| label: fig-line-parallel-hp
#| fig-cap: "First-angle projections of AB: the top view has true length 8 units at 45° to XY; the front view is horizontal and 5.66 units long. Dashed projectors align corresponding endpoints."
#| fig-alt: "Front view a prime b prime above XY, horizontal and dimensioned 5.66 units; top view ab below XY, sloping down to the right at 45 degrees and dimensioned 8 units. Vertical dashed projectors connect matching endpoints."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-dpi: 160
#| echo: false

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import Arc

length = 8.0
phi_deg = 45.0  # true inclination to VP; theta (inclination to HP) = 0
phi = np.deg2rad(phi_deg)

# Physical coordinates: x along XY, y in front of VP, z above HP.
A = np.array([2.0, 2.0, 3.0])
B = A + np.array([length * np.cos(phi), length * np.sin(phi), 0.0])
points = np.vstack([A, B])

# Unfold HP downwards in first-angle projection: plan ordinate = -y.
plan = points[:, [0, 1]] * np.array([1.0, -1.0])
elevation = points[:, [0, 2]]
front_length = np.linalg.norm(elevation[1] - elevation[0])

# Check the geometry before drawing the illustration.
assert np.isclose(np.linalg.norm(B - A), length)
assert np.isclose(np.linalg.norm(plan[1] - plan[0]), length)
assert np.allclose(plan[:, 0], elevation[:, 0])
assert np.isclose(elevation[0, 1], elevation[1, 1])
assert np.isclose(front_length, length * np.cos(phi))
assert np.isclose(np.rad2deg(np.arctan2(
    -(plan[1, 1] - plan[0, 1]), plan[1, 0] - plan[0, 0]
)), phi_deg)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 9))
front_color, plan_color = "#b45309", "#1d4ed8"
construction_color = "#6b7280"

# Shared XY reference and projectors, perpendicular to XY.
ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=1.2)
ax.text(-0.3, 0.2, "X", ha="center", fontsize=12)
ax.text(9.3, 0.2, "Y", ha="center", fontsize=12)
ax.text(4.8, 0.25, "XY reference line", ha="center", fontsize=10)
for top, front in zip(plan, elevation):
    ax.plot([top[0], front[0]], [top[1], front[1]],
            color=construction_color, linestyle="--", linewidth=0.9, zorder=1)

ax.plot(*elevation.T, "o-", color=front_color, linewidth=2.2, zorder=3)
ax.plot(*plan.T, "o-", color=plan_color, linewidth=2.2, zorder=3)
for point, label, offset in [
    (elevation[0], "$a'$", (-12, 10)),
    (elevation[1], "$b'$", (12, 10)),
    (plan[0], "$a$", (-12, -8)),
    (plan[1], "$b$", (12, -3)),
]:
    ax.annotate(label, point, textcoords="offset points", xytext=offset,
                ha="center", fontsize=13)


def dimension(start, end, offset, label, rotation=0):
    """Offset dimension with extension lines; all coordinates use drawing units."""
    shift = np.asarray(offset)
    p, q = start + shift, end + shift
    for original, shifted in [(start, p), (end, q)]:
        ax.plot([original[0], shifted[0]], [original[1], shifted[1]],
                color=construction_color, linewidth=0.8)
    ax.annotate("", xy=q, xytext=p,
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="<->", color="black", linewidth=0.9,
                                shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0))
    midpoint = (p + q) / 2
    ax.text(*midpoint, label, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=10,
            rotation=rotation, rotation_mode="anchor",
            bbox=dict(facecolor="white", edgecolor="none", pad=2.5))


dimension(elevation[0], elevation[1], [0.0, 1.1],
          f"$a'b' = 8\\cos45^\\circ = {front_length:.2f}$ units")
# Offset the true-length dimension perpendicular to the top view.
dimension(plan[0], plan[1], [-0.55, -0.55],
          "$ab = 8$ units (true length)", rotation=-phi_deg)

# Measure the inclination against a local reference parallel to XY, at a.
radius = 1.35
ax.plot([plan[0, 0], plan[0, 0] + 2.4], [plan[0, 1], plan[0, 1]],
        color=construction_color, linestyle="-.", linewidth=0.8)
ax.add_patch(Arc(plan[0], 2 * radius, 2 * radius,
                 theta1=-phi_deg, theta2=0, color="black", linewidth=1.0))
angle_position = plan[0] + 1.9 * np.array([
    np.cos(-phi / 2), np.sin(-phi / 2)
])
ax.text(*angle_position, "$\\phi=45^\\circ$", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=11,
        bbox=dict(facecolor="white", edgecolor="none", pad=1.0))

ax.text(4.8, 5.2, "Front view (elevation)", ha="center", fontsize=13,
        color=front_color, weight="bold")
ax.text(4.8, 2.25, "$a'b'\\parallel XY$; inclination to HP: $\\theta=0^\\circ$",
        ha="center", fontsize=11)
ax.text(6.3, -3.0, "Top view (plan)", ha="center", fontsize=13,
        color=plan_color, weight="bold")
ax.text(6.3, -3.55, "True length and true inclination to VP",
        ha="center", fontsize=10)

ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")
ax.set_xlim(-0.8, 9.8)
ax.set_ylim(-9.0, 5.8)
ax.axis("off")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The projectors confirm that $a$ and $a'$ share one horizontal position,
and $b$ and $b'$ share the other. In this first-angle drawing the top view
slopes downwards because B is farther in front of VP; the magnitude of its
angle to XY is still 45°. The locations relative to XY represent distances
from the projection planes, not additional inclinations of the line.
